contentHtml:
What Twinkeep is

The same shot saved four times — once from your camera, once from a text, twice from an export. Twinkeep finds duplicate photos, videos, and audio on your Mac, quarantines the byte-identical extras for you, and brings you only the judgment calls.

It is three tools in one native app: a duplicate media cleaner, File Rules that watch folders and file new arrivals automatically, and Maintain utilities for everyday housekeeping. Everything runs on your Mac. No account, no telemetry, no subscription — one purchase.

You only review what is actually in doubt

Byte-identical files are matched by content, and their extras go straight to Quarantine. A thousand of them take no more of your time than one. Review is kept for the genuine maybes — the same shot re-cropped, re-exported, or resaved — where only you can say which to keep.

When one does need your eye, Twinkeep puts both copies on screen at full size, side by side, with zoom and pan moving together down to 100% pixels and a strip between them calling out exactly what differs: dimensions, file size, format, camera, date. One key decides it.

Nothing disappears

Every removal goes to Quarantine first — never straight to delete. Restore anything, any time, back to exactly where it came from. Browse it as a list, icons, gallery, or filmstrip. Emptying it permanently is the one action Twinkeep will not do without asking.

What we fixed, and why

Version 1.1 is mostly the result of going back through the app and asking what it was quietly getting wrong. Some of it is uncomfortable to write down, so here it is plainly.

  • Junk Sweep could delete your crash reports. It listed the folder macOS writes crash and hang reports into as “safe to clean”, and pre-selected it — which meant a routine cleanup quietly destroyed the same reports the Stability tool reads. That folder is now permanently off limits, with a test that fails if anyone ever puts it back.
  • Three tools said “nothing found” when they meant “I cannot look”. On the App Store build, Downloads Dust, Disk Analysis and Stability showed empty results when macOS had not granted folder access — indistinguishable from a clean Mac. They now say access is needed and offer to ask for it.
  • Memory Relief overstated what it freed. Quitting is a request an app can decline; one with unsaved changes stays open. Twinkeep counted those as freed memory. It now waits to see what actually closed and reports only that.
  • File Rules started working before you asked it to. It now ships switched off. Nothing on your Mac moves until you turn it on.
  • Folder sizes ignored hidden files, so the amount Junk Sweep promised was less than it actually reclaimed. Totals now include them.
  • The background stability monitor rewrote its entire history every minute. Now it appends a line.

None of that is exciting. All of it is the difference between a utility you can trust with your files and one you cannot.

Duplicate cleaning

  • Exact duplicates — SHA-256 content hashing finds byte-identical files whatever they are named; extras are quarantined for you automatically, and you can switch that off
  • Similar photos — perceptual matching groups the same shot re-cropped, re-exported or resaved, and always waits for your decision
  • Photos, video, and audio in one scanner
  • Scan any folders you choose, including external drives
  • Smart keep policy — prefers Live Photo and HEIC originals over copy-like names, then the older file and the shorter path
  • Speed modes and a hash index so rescans stay fast

File Rules — the folder that keeps itself tidy

Cleanup apps tidy once. File Rules stops the mess coming back. Point it at Downloads, the Desktop, or any folder you choose, and new arrivals get filed the moment they land — sixteen ways to match, nine things to do, including rules that act on whether a file is already a duplicate of something you keep. Folder automation like this is normally an app you buy separately.

Maintain — everyday Mac housekeeping

  • Junk Sweep — caches, logs, and Xcode build junk, sorted by risk
  • Downloads Dust — old files still sitting in Downloads
  • Disk Analysis — which folders are actually using your space
  • Storage Pulse — capacity and free space, including what macOS holds as purgeable
  • Memory Relief — which apps are using the most memory, and quit the ones you choose
  • Stability — crash reports in plain English, with an optional local CPU and memory history

Requirements

  • macOS 13 or later
  • Apple Silicon or Intel

Privacy & safety

Every scan runs on your Mac. Nothing is uploaded, there is no account and no telemetry. Keep a current backup of anything irreplaceable before any cleanup tool touches it — Twinkeep moves files you approve, and quarantines exact duplicates automatically unless you switch that off. See the in-app EULA and Disclaimer.

Native SwiftUI · CryptoKit hashing · App sandbox with user-selected folders

The direct download from this page includes a 7-day trial that unlocks in the app, after which you enter a license key. The Mac App Store version is a paid app with no trial, so buying there licenses it immediately. Both cost $9.99 once.

Not without you asking. Every removal goes to Quarantine first and can be restored at any time to exactly where it came from. Emptying Quarantine permanently is the one action Twinkeep will not do without confirming.

faqs.q: Do my photos get uploaded anywhere?
faqs.a: No. Every scan runs on your Mac. There is no account, no telemetry and no cloud upload of your media. Twinkeep runs in the App Sandbox with access only to folders you select.

faqs.q: How does Twinkeep decide what is a duplicate?
faqs.a: Byte-identical files are matched by SHA-256 content hash regardless of filename, and their extras are quarantined automatically unless you switch that off. Similar photos — the same shot re-cropped, re-exported or resaved — are grouped by perceptual matching and always wait for your decision.

faqs.q: Can Twinkeep scan an external drive?
faqs.a: Yes. You choose which folders to scan, including folders on external drives, and a hash index keeps rescans fast.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Mac App Store and the direct version?

name: PrecisDesk
shortDescription: Screen capture, screen recording and window management for the Mac, in one native app — with webcam picture-in-picture, on-device captions, and window layouts that survive unplugging a monitor.
contentHtml:
What PrecisDesk is

PrecisDesk (PREH-sis-desk) is a screen capture, screen recording and window manager for the Mac, in one native app. Take a shot, record a walkthrough, or put every window where it belongs — without learning three separate tools.

Everything runs on your Mac. Nothing you capture is uploaded, there is no account, and there are no analytics or advertising SDKs.

Who it’s for

Mac users who live in screenshots, demos and multi-monitor layouts — support and QA teams, founders recording walkthroughs, and anyone who docks a laptop and rebuilds their windows twice a day.

Capture

  • Capture an area, a single window, or a whole screen
  • Quick Access overlay after every capture — annotate, copy, print, reveal or delete
  • Save folders you choose and filename templates you control
  • History of every capture, filterable, with a retention period

Annotate and redact

  • Crop, arrows, lines, shapes, freehand, text, highlighter and step counters
  • Spotlight, blur and pixelate — redaction applied to the exported image, not drawn on top
  • On-device OCR (Apple Vision) to copy text out of any capture
  • Colour picker in hex or RGB
  • Non-destructive projects, plus PNG export

Screen recording

  • Record a display or a region to MP4, or export an animated GIF
  • Microphone and system audio, independently switchable
  • Cursor, click highlights and on-screen keystrokes for walkthroughs
  • Pause and resume — pauses are stitched out, not frozen into the file
  • Hide PrecisDesk while recording so the app never appears in the video

Webcam picture-in-picture

  • Burn the camera in as you record, or place it afterwards in the editor
  • Any corner or anywhere you drag it, in a circle or a rounded rectangle, with a border
  • Move it partway through so it never covers what matters, or hide it for a stretch

Captions

  • Generate captions from the recording’s own audio, on-device (Apple Speech)
  • Edit the wording and retime any line
  • Burn them into the video, or export a separate .srt

Clip editor

  • Trim the ends, cut sections out of the middle, split and mute
  • Compare Edited against Original before you commit
  • Non-destructive — your source recording is never overwritten

Windows

  • Halves, quarters, thirds and sixths, maximize, centre and grid placement
  • Keyboard shortcuts for everything, plus an on-screen snap palette and drag-to-edge zones
  • Put my windows back — remembers your arrangement per set of monitors and restores it when a display is unplugged and plugged back in
  • Saved per-app layouts, size cycling, ignored apps, and gaps between tiled windows
  • Switcher with live window previews, grouped by app, with search and up to nine of your own shortcuts
  • URL commands such as precisdesk://snap/leftHalf

Privacy and permissions

PrecisDesk asks for Screen Recording, and — only if you use those features — Microphone, Camera, Speech Recognition, and Accessibility for moving other apps’ windows. You can decline or revoke any of them; features that depend on a permission you decline simply do not run.

Requirements

  • macOS 14 or later
  • Apple Silicon or Intel, native

faqs.q: Does PrecisDesk upload my screenshots or recordings?
faqs.a: No. Captures, recordings, text recognition and speech recognition all run on your Mac. There is no account system and no media server.

faqs.q: Why does it need Accessibility permission?
faqs.a: Moving and resizing another app’s windows requires the macOS Accessibility permission. Decline it and the capture and recording features still work — only window management needs it.

faqs.q: Can it put my windows back after I unplug a monitor?
faqs.a: Yes. PrecisDesk remembers your arrangement for each set of displays and can restore it when that set comes back. It ships switched off, because it moves windows you did not ask it to move.
Pricing is being finalised for the 1.0 release.
macOS 14 or later, native on Apple Silicon and Intel.
